q: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as "____" due to their link with organisms.
e: Organic compounds are primarily composed of carbon and hydrogen and are fundamental to biological processes.

q: These enormous molecules are termed ____; they are formed by smaller molecules connecting together as if they were holding hands.
e: Macromolecules are large structures like carbohydrates, proteins, and nucleic acids essential for life.

q: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called ____.
e: Hydrocarbons form the basic backbone for more complex organic molecules.

q: Ethers can be used as organic solvents in the perfumery and ____ industries.
e: Ethers are volatile and often possess pleasant odours, making them useful in aroma and perfume formulations.

q: Carboxylic acids are present in many common household items such as vinegar (____ acid).
e: Acetic acid is the primary carboxylic acid responsible for the sour taste and pungent smell of vinegar.

q: Some other organic compounds contain nitrogen atoms, such as amines and ____.
e: Amides and amines are key nitrogen-containing functional groups in organic chemistry and biology.

q: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two ____ groups.
e: The general structure of an ether is R-O-R', where R and R' are alkyl or aryl groups.

q: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the ____.
e: Symmetrical ethers have identical groups attached to the oxygen atom, such as dimethyl ether.

q: Ethers have the general formula ____.
e: This formula represents saturated, non-cyclic ethers, which are isomeric with aliphatic alcohols.

q: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group are named as an ____ substituent.
e: The smaller chain attached to the oxygen is treated as an alkoxy group attached to the parent alkane.

q: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of ____ from two molecules of alcohol.
e: This dehydration reaction typically requires an acid catalyst and controlled heating.

q: There is no intermolecular ____ bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much lower than alcohol of similar molecular mass.
e: Ethers lack an O-H bond, preventing them from forming hydrogen bonds with each other.

q: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and ____.
e: Hydrogen iodide is a strong acid that cleaves the ether linkage to yield an alcohol and an alkyl iodide.

q: Ethoxyethane (diethyl ether), the most common member of the ether family, was used for many years as a surgical ____ agent.
e: Diethyl ether was historically significant in medicine for inducing general anaesthesia.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the ____ group, >C=O.
e: The carbonyl group consists of a carbon atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom.

q: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one ____ atom.
e: This structural feature distinguishes aldehydes from ketones, where the carbonyl carbon is bonded to two other carbons.

q: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula ____.
e: This formula applies to saturated, aliphatic aldehydes and ketones containing one carbonyl group.

q: The common names of aldehydes are given based on the names of corresponding ____ acids.
e: For example, formaldehyde corresponds to formic acid, and acetaldehyde to acetic acid.

q: An alpha ($\alpha$) carbon is a carbon atom bonded to a ____ group.
e: In common nomenclature, Greek letters are used to designate the position of substituents relative to the functional group.

q: The systematic (IUPAC) names are derived from the names of the parent ____.
e: The longest carbon chain containing the functional group determines the parent hydrocarbon name.

q: The suffix ____ instead of e is added to the characteristic stem for aldehydes.
e: Replacing the 'e' of the parent alkane with '-al' designates the molecule as an aldehyde.

q: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ____, respectively, when oxidised.
e: Oxidation of primary alcohols yields aldehydes, while secondary alcohols yield ketones.

q: The aldehyde product is obtained by ____ to remove it immediately from the reaction mixture.
e: Distillation prevents the aldehyde from being further oxidised into a carboxylic acid.

q: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of $H_2SO_4$ and ____ produces ethanal.
e: Mercuric sulfate acts as a catalyst in the hydration of alkynes to form carbonyl compounds.

q: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to ____ acids with common oxidising agents.
e: The presence of the hydrogen atom on the carbonyl carbon makes aldehydes susceptible to oxidation.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding primary and secondary alcohols, using the reducing agent lithium aluminium hydride, ____.
e: Lithium aluminium hydride is a strong reducing agent capable of reducing carbonyl groups to hydroxyl groups.

q: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as ____.
e: This nucleophilic addition reaction forms cyanohydrins, also known as hydroxynitriles.

q: Formalin (40% aqueous solution of methanal) is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological ____.
e: Formaldehyde cross-links proteins, effectively preserving tissue structures in biological specimens.

q: Ketones are popular solvents for other moderately polar substances, including waxes, plastics, paints, lacquers, varnishes, and ____.
e: Propanone (acetone) is a widely used ketone solvent due to its ability to dissolve many organic compounds.

q: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group ____.
e: The carboxyl group combines a carbonyl (>C=O) and a hydroxyl (-OH) group on the same carbon atom.

q: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a ____ group.
e: The combination of these two groups gives carboxylic acids their characteristic acidic properties.

q: They form a homologous series with the general formula ____.
e: This formula represents saturated, monocarboxylic acids.

q: Formic acid was obtained by distillation of ants (Latin formica, meaning "____").
e: Many common names for carboxylic acids derive from their natural biological sources.

q: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the "____" location position in numbering.
e: The carboxyl carbon is automatically assigned position 1 in IUPAC nomenclature.

q: Ethanoic acid is formed by the oxidation of ____.
e: Ethanol, a primary alcohol, oxidises first to ethanal and then to ethanoic acid.

q: Instead of a distillation set, a ____ condenser has to be used so that the volatile components remain in the reaction for long enough to complete their reaction.
e: Refluxing ensures complete oxidation of the primary alcohol to the carboxylic acid without losing volatile intermediates.

q: Ethanol is oxidised by atmospheric oxygen in the presence of bacteria (____).
e: Acetobacter species are responsible for the natural fermentation of ethanol into vinegar.

q: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals such as sodium, potassium, and magnesium to give salt and ____.
e: Like other acids, carboxylic acids release hydrogen gas when reacting with active metals.

q: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and ____.
e: This reaction produces effervescence, which is a standard test for the carboxyl functional group.

q: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using the reducing agent, $LiAlH_4$, in dry ____ at room temperature.
e: Dry ether is used as a solvent because $LiAlH_4$ reacts violently with water.

q: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of ____ acid.
e: Aspirin is chemically known as acetylsalicylic acid.

q: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl (-OH) group has been replaced by an ____ (-OR) group.
e: The substitution of the acidic hydrogen with an alkyl group forms an ester.

q: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as ____.
e: Fischer esterification is an acid-catalysed condensation reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol.

q: Acidic hydrolysis is simply the reverse of ____.
e: Heating an ester with aqueous acid breaks it back down into its parent carboxylic acid and alcohol.

q: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, such as aqueous sodium hydroxide, it is fully ____.
e: Base-promoted hydrolysis, or saponification, is irreversible and goes to completion.

q: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an acid ____.
e: Transesterification exchanges the alkyl group of an ester with that of another alcohol.

q: Naturally-occurring esters (animal fats or vegetable oil) mixed with NaOH produce ____ that is used for washing dishes and clothes.
e: The saponification of triglycerides yields glycerol and fatty acid salts, commonly known as soap.

q: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia have been replaced by ____ groups.
e: Amines are considered organic derivatives of ammonia.

q: Amines are classified as primary ($1^\circ$), secondary ($2^\circ$), and tertiary ($3^\circ$), depending on how many alkyl groups are attached to the ____.
e: The degree of substitution on the nitrogen atom determines the classification of the amine.

q: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in ____ in a sealed tube.
e: Ethanolic ammonia is used to facilitate the nucleophilic substitution reaction.

q: Because more hydrogen bonds are formed in primary amines, they are more soluble in water than secondary and ____ amines.
e: Tertiary amines lack N-H bonds and cannot act as hydrogen bond donors to water.

q: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell; this reaction is known as ____ reaction.
e: The carbylamine test is a specific chemical test used to identify primary amines.

q: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by $-NH_2$, -NHR, or ____ of an amine.
e: Amides can be primary, secondary, or tertiary depending on the substitution on the nitrogen atom.

q: The addition of ammonia ($NH_3$) to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a ____ reaction.
e: The reaction involves the elimination of a water molecule upon heating the intermediate ammonium salt.

q: Generally, amides can be hydrolysed in either acidic or ____ solutions.
e: Hydrolysis of amides requires harsh conditions, such as prolonged heating with strong acids or bases.
